report.body:
Civil and military police in Água Clara, in Mato Grosso do Sul, arrested five
men and seized marijuana and cocaine. Four were arrested in the act for
drug trafficking and association for trafficking, and the fifth was detained
under an open arrest warrant. The operation began on the night of 4
November 2026 with an anonymous tip about a car used to sell drugs in Água
Clara. The tip named a white VW Gol selling drugs in the Jardim das
Palmeiras neighbourhood. The driver fled when the patrol car approached but
was caught after a chase of a few blocks. Officers found cocaine in the car
and, at the man's home, marijuana, a precision scale, packaging material and
cash.

The first suspect was already under investigation by the Civil Police's General
Investigations Section (SIG). A joint military and civil police task force
then located two other suspects at a snack bar, according to the local account. At a second address used to store drugs, officers found 59 tablets of
marijuana weighing about 54 kg. Two men, aged 18 and 20, were arrested in
the act at that address. A third suspect, aged 22, was found with about 500
g of marijuana and a precision scale. Police also recovered 120 g of
cocaine in 19 portions during the follow-up inquiries. The cocaine had been
discarded by the first suspect during the military police approach, according to
the investigation.

The operation's final tally was about 54.64 kg of drugs, marijuana and cocaine
together. Police also took a car, a motorcycle, three precision scales,
three mobile phones, packaging and about R$250 in cash. The local portal
described the storage site as a drug hideout in a wooded area near the MS-324. The detainees were taken to the Água Clara civil police station for legal
procedures.

The New Cairo Criminal Court, sitting in the Fifth Settlement, sentenced a woman
worker to six years of aggravated imprisonment for possessing hashish for sale
in the Badr police district. The court was presided over by Counsellor
Wajih Hamza Shaqwir, with counsellors Yasser Mohamed Youssef, Sameh Abdel Ghani
al-Antabli and Sherif Sami Ali al-Saeed, and court clerks Wael Farraj and
Mahmoud Abdel Rashid. The referral order said she held the hashish for sale
in the Badr police district on 22 April 2026 without legal authorisation.

An investigations assistant at Badr police station said he saw her showing signs
of suspicion at a security checkpoint in the district and asked to search her
belongings, and she agreed. He said the search found 125 brown pieces of
hashish, a sum of money and a mobile phone.

According to his account, she admitted holding the drugs for sale, that the
money came from her activity and that the phone was for contacting her
customers. A chemical laboratory report found that 30 of the 125 pieces
were examined and identified the material as hashish, with a stated weight of 9
kilograms and 350 grams.

report.body:
Sohag Criminal Court sentenced three men to death by hanging for possessing
hashish for trade and for carrying a scalpel (mishrat), a bladed tool, without
legal justification in Al-Maragha district. The court also ordered the
three to pay the costs and confiscated the seized items. Counsellor Hamdi
Abdel Aziz headed the panel, with Counsellors Mohyi Abu Kreisha and Amr Makki as
members.

The three are identified in the reports by the initials M. A., 35, a
technical-diploma holder, M. M., 25, also a technical-diploma holder, and A. A.,
41, unemployed. The Public Prosecution charged them with possessing and
acquiring the hashish for trade and with using cars to transport and promote the
drug.

The case dates to November 2025 in Al-Maragha district, Sohag governorate.
Ahl Masr reported that officers of the Anti-Narcotics General Administration for
the Middle Upper Egypt region, Sohag branch, arrested the men after the
prosecution issued a warrant to search the first defendant. A chemical
laboratory report found the seized material was brown and confirmed as hashish
in three lots of 80, 150 and 50 pieces, 280 in all, and a plastic sack carried
traces of the drug. The prosecution's inspection of a seized car found the
drugs in a place under the first defendant's control.

The case was registered as No 16693 of 2025 for Al-Maragha and No 3346 of 2025
for North Sohag, Ahl Masr reported. All three men are from Al-Ghanayim
centre in Asyut governorate, Ahl Masr reported. The court referred the case
to the Grand Mufti for a religious opinion on the death sentences. After
the Mufti's opinion arrived, the court issued the final death sentence for all
three, by the unanimous view of the panel, Ahl Masr reported.

report.body:
Mossos d'Esquadra officers arrested seven men aged between 29 and 55 at an
industrial warehouse in Cabanes on 1 October 2026, on suspicion of belonging to
a drug-trafficking organisation. The seven were brought before the Secció
Civil i d'Instrucció of the Tribunal de Instància de Figueres. Four were
held in provisional prison without bail and bail was set for the other three.

Inside, officers found the seven unloading pallets from an articulated lorry's
trailer, intending to load the hashish into vans for distribution. The
hashish was hidden in the lorry's legal cargo inside large raffia sacks filled
with rubber crumb, a method used to defeat police and customs checks. The
Mossos seized 8,025 kg of hashish. The force valued the haul at more than
16.2 million euros on the illegal market. Officers also found a firearm in
one of the suspects' vans.

The investigation began in June 2026 after officers intercepted a van carrying
about 2,400 kg of hashish in Viladecans, Barcelona province, and traced its load
to the Cabanes warehouse. Surveillance teams saw people and vehicles arrive
at the building without any business or work activity taking place. On the
day of the raid they watched several people replace the vehicles' original
number plates with others fixed using zip ties. The 8,025 kg is more than
half of the 14.9 tonnes of hashish the Mossos had seized across Catalonia in
2026 up to that point, El Caso reported. The investigation remains open and
further arrests have not been ruled out.

report.body:
Mossos d'Esquadra officers from the DIC arrested seven men aged between 29 and
55 on 1 October 2026 on suspicion of belonging to a drug-trafficking
organisation. The operation took place at an industrial warehouse in
Cabanes, in the Alt Empordà, where officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish. The
hashish was hidden among merchandise in the trailer of an articulated lorry,
inside large raffia sacks filled with rubber crumbs to make detection harder at
police and customs checks. Officers entering the building found the seven
men unloading pallets from the trailer, intending to load the hashish into
several vans for distribution.

The investigation began in June 2026 after officers in Viladecans, in the Baix
Llobregat, intercepted a van carrying nearly 2,400 kg of hashish, a case taken
up by the Gavà court. The narcotics group of the DIC in Sant Feliu de
Llobregat traced that load to a warehouse in Cabanes used only for storing and
distributing drugs. Mossos valued the hashish at more than 16.2 million
euros on the illegal market. The force said the seizure was a significant
part of the nearly 14,900 kg of hashish it had confiscated so far in 2026 and
among its largest operations. The warehouse was almost entirely open-plan,
with nothing to indicate business or residential use, the Mossos said.

During the search officers also found a firearm in one of the detainees' vans. The seven were brought before the Civil and Instruction Section of the
Tribunal de Instancia in Figueres. Four of the seven were remanded in
prison without bail and the other three were granted bail. The
investigation remains open and further arrests have not been ruled out.

report.title: Driver arrested in Ceuta port as 300 kg hashish found in truck
report.summary: Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta after finding a hidden compartment packed with bags of hashish. Outlets estimate the haul at about 300 kilograms, pending an official weighing.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure. Officers used hammers, shears, sledgehammers and an angle grinder to break open the metal sheet protecting the compartment. The hashish was hidden in a compartment built behind the cabin and at the end of the cargo section.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On Sunday 15 November the driver was brought before the court, which ordered him held in preventive prison on a charge of an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remains open on suspicion of larger consignments and of heavy vehicles being hidden in spaces used as stash houses for hashish.

report.body:
Spain's National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma and seized 60
kilos of hashish and weapons from them. The National Police detained the
five for drug trafficking and membership of a criminal group.

The investigation began when officers learned of a parcel of hashish addressed
to a man who lived in Palma. The parcel contained 24 kilos of hashish, and
officers arrested the addressee on suspicion of drug trafficking. A search
of his home found another 36 kilos of hashish, an air rifle with a silencer and
about 10,000 euros in cash. The man and a woman were arrested there as
suspected authors of drug trafficking and membership of a criminal group. A
second suspect, said to have been in charge of storing and transporting drugs,
was arrested and his home searched. There officers found two kilos of
cocaine, doses of the drug, cutting agent, a pistol with 9mm cartridges and a
bow with arrows. They also found a hydraulic press used, police suspect, to
compress the cocaine. A fifth person was arrested for being connected to
the case.

The operation was run by Group I of the National Police's drugs squad, which had
been investigating for months. Police suspect the hashish was distributed
to others for sale on a smaller scale, and say the investigation remains open
with further arrests not ruled out. Officers from the Prevention and
Reaction Unit, Group II of the drugs squad and the canine unit took part in the
searches.

report.body:
Officers of the National Police's Drugs and Organised Crime Unit (Udyco)
arrested at least three people on Mallorca who were storing almost 50 kilos of
hashish for sale. The National Police put the operation at five arrests, four men and one woman. The suspects received the hashish from the Spanish
mainland in courier parcels, according to the newspaper's case sources. The intercepted parcel, addressed to a man living in Palma, contained 24 kilograms of hashish. The
arrests took place on Wednesday 4 November. Officers searched a home in
Marratxí, a municipality east of Palma, and another in a town in es Raiguer, the
district around the town of Inca. Officers from the prevention and reaction unit, Group II of the drug squad and canine handlers took part in the searches. At the second home, that of a suspect who allegedly stored and transported the drugs, officers found 2 kilograms of cocaine, cutting agent, a 9mm pistol with cartridges, a bow with arrows and a hydraulic press. An investigating court in Palma declared
the case secret. Investigators had followed the suspects for some time;
over the previous months they had collected parcels of the drug from courier
companies and kept them at home for sale through others in the network.

In the Marratxí search, police found a large quantity of hashish in a chest
freezer and an air rifle. The force put the hashish seized in the operation at 60 kilograms, along with weapons. The home of the main suspect held 36 kilograms of hashish, an air rifle with a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash. A woman was arrested there over her alleged link
to the criminal organisation and was released at the police station hours later. The five were held on suspicion of drug trafficking and of belonging to a criminal group or organisation. Two more people were arrested the same day, and all the suspects are
Spanish nationals.

The investigation is still open, further arrests are not ruled out, and the
suspects were due to appear before a Palma court in the coming hours.

report.body:
Customs officers stopped a Renault Talisman at a roundabout in Saint-Lary-Soulan
at 22:15 on 28 September 2026. The car was coming back from Spain through
the Aragnouet-Bielsa tunnel. The driver was a Ukrainian national living in
Poland with no previous criminal record. Under a carpet that was not
original, officers found two metal compartments holding 32 heat-sealed bags of
cannabis herb, 32.800 kg in total. They also found cloths soaked in white
spirit, used to mask the smell of the drug, and 405 euros in cash. La
Dépêche put the estimated value of the haul at 131,200 euros.

The car had been located two days earlier in Barcelona and then Tarragona, and
crossed the border at Aragnouet shortly after 21:30 that night. A phone
found on board, which the driver said was not his, showed passages at Aragnouet
on 13 August and 4 September, without establishing that they were other missions
by the same driver. The driver told the court he was paid 3,000 euros to
collect the cannabis in Alicante and take it to Poland, after being contacted on
Telegram by someone he did not know.

He was tried in immediate appearance at the criminal court in Tarbes on 1
October 2026. The court sentenced him to 24 months in prison and a 10-year
ban from French territory. It fined him 131,200 euros for transporting
narcotics without a valid supporting document and 405 euros for customs money
laundering, 131,605 euros in total. The court also ordered the confiscation
of the 32.8 kg of cannabis, the 405 euros, two phones and a computer. The
two-year term was pronounced with a committal order, and a conditional release
with expulsion was proposed as a sentence adjustment. The prosecutor had
sought two years in prison.

Immigration police and officials of the Department of Thai Traditional and
Alternative Medicine searched a rented three-storey house on Soi Khu Bon 27 in
Tha Raeng, Bang Khen district, Bangkok, on 19 October 2026. The search was
carried out under a warrant issued by the Min Buri Criminal Court. Inside,
officers found one Vietnamese national and four Myanmar nationals sorting
cannabis flowers for packing and delivery to customers, and arrested them.
Black bags of cannabis buds were hidden on all three floors, with a total weight
of more than five tonnes.

The raid followed complaints from neighbours about the smell of cannabis, and
officers spent about two months gathering evidence before the search.
Neighbours endured the smell for weeks before alerting the authorities. The
house covered about 100 square wah and had a ventilation pipe system installed
to carry the smell outside. A Thai national signed the lease for the house,
and the foreigners had lived and worked there for more than a year. The
four Myanmar workers were paid about 200 to 300 baht a day. Police
suspected the Vietnamese man was supervising an operation run like a company.

The operators held a cannabis licence from Nong Bua Lamphu province that did not
cover Bangkok, a legal officer of the Department of Thai Traditional and
Alternative Medicine said. Under the Thai traditional medicine protection
law, selling or processing cannabis flowers without permission for the location
carries up to one year in prison or a fine of up to 20,000 baht. Police
said the seized cannabis would be sent to a laboratory to establish whether it
was grown in Thailand or imported. Investigators were also tracing the Thai
tenant, the source of the cannabis and any financiers behind the operation.
The five were taken into custody for legal action, and police said they were
widening the investigation to the network behind the operation.

report.body:
Construction worker Mehmet Arıcan disappeared in Taşpınar Mahallesi, in the
Mustafakemalpaşa district of Bursa, on 7 September 2010 after leaving the place
where he worked. His body was found four days later at Karanlıkdere, and
investigators determined that he had been shot dead with a hunting rifle in the
forest. Three suspects were detained at the time, but a decision was taken
not to prosecute them and the file was placed on permanent search.

The killing was solved 16 years later. The Mustafakemalpaşa chief public
prosecutor's office re-examined phone records, financial investigations and new
witness statements in the case. On 11 November, Jasat teams, the
gendarmerie's crime investigation unit, raided eight addresses at the same time
and caught 17 suspects. A court in Mustafakemalpaşa remanded one suspect,
identified only as H.F., and the other 16 were released.

Investigators found that Arıcan and H.F. had been in a feud at the time over
entering a hemp field without permission.

report.body:
The Saratoga County Sheriff's Office said deputies seized 489 pounds of cannabis
after a traffic stop on the Northway in Clifton Park. The two men had been
travelling on Interstate 87 in Clifton Park when deputies stopped their vehicle
at about 2:28 p.m. Deputies stopped them for following too closely and for
insufficient tail lamps.

The investigation led to the arrests of Kevin C. Wilbur, 46, of Brushton, and
Quinton L. Carle, 23, of Bombay. Both were charged with criminal possession
of cannabis in the first degree, a class D felony. Wilbur was also cited
for following too closely and for having insufficient tail lamps.

Both men were arraigned before Judge Jennifer Jeram in Clifton Park Town Court. Wilbur was remanded to the Saratoga County Jail, and Carle was released on
his own recognizance pending further proceedings in that court.

Wilbur and Carle are accused of knowingly and unlawfully possessing 489 pounds
of cannabis. Sheriff Jeffrey R. Brown said his deputies had prevented
nearly one-quarter ton of illicit cannabis from reaching the streets.
